deep.reconstruction:
Setting. pi is the profinite fundamental group of P^1 minus {0,1,inf}, written K on this page. It is free profinite on the inertia generators l_0, l_1, l_inf, subject to l_0 l_1 l_inf = 1. Grothendieck studies the extension E of S_3 by pi inside Aut(pi), generated by inner automorphisms and lifts sigma_0, sigma_1, sigma_inf of the three transpositions. In modern terms E is the orbifold fundamental group of the quotient orbifold [(P^1 - {0,1,inf})/S_3], the j-line, which is the profinite completion of PSL_2(Z) = Z/2 * Z/3. The subgroup pi corresponds to Gamma(2)/±1, the quotient is PSL_2(Z)/Gamma(2) = S_3, and the three cusps 0,1,inf map to the single cusp j = inf with ramification index 2. Hence the 'groupes de ramification' at 0,1,inf in E contain square roots eps_i of the inertia l_i (previous page).

This page normalises eps_inf. sigma_inf swaps l_0 and l_1, so sigma_inf(l_inf) = l_0^{-1} l_1^{-1}. Then int(l_0) sigma_inf sends l_0 to l_0 l_1 l_0^{-1} and l_1 to l_0, and fixes l_inf: this is the displayed formula. It lies in the stabiliser of l_inf, but its square in E is int(l_0 sigma_inf(l_0)) = l_0 l_1 = l_inf^{-1}, not l_inf.

So Grothendieck multiplies on the right by l_inf^alpha (alpha in Z-hat). He adopts the convention of writing g for int(g), so that K sits inside Aut(K), and sets eps_inf = l_0 sigma_inf l_inf^alpha. Then:
- eps_inf^2 = l_0 sigma_inf(l_inf^alpha l_0) l_inf^alpha = l_0 (l_0^{-1} l_1^{-1})^alpha l_1 (l_1^{-1} l_0^{-1})^alpha.
- Since l_0 (l_1 l_0)^{-alpha} l_0^{-1} = (l_0 l_1)^{-alpha} = l_inf^alpha, this equals l_inf^{2 alpha - 1}.
- The condition eps_inf^2 = l_inf therefore forces alpha = 1.

He verifies this by a word computation. A first expansion is crossed out ('Non !'); a corrected one is marked 'OK': l_0 l_1 l_0 l_0^{-1} l_1^{-1} l_1 l_1^{-1} l_0^{-1} = 1.

Conclusion: eps_inf = l_0 sigma_inf l_inf, i.e. int(l_0) sigma_inf int(l_inf). By cyclic symmetry (0 to 1 to inf), eps_0 = l_1 sigma_0 l_0 and eps_1 = l_inf sigma_1 l_1. On the next page these become a new generating system eps_0, eps_1, eps_inf for E, with eps_i^2 = l_i.

In modern dictionary terms, eps_i are parabolic generators of PSL_2(Z) of cusp width 2 relative to Gamma(2). Equivalently, they are images in B_3/Z = PSL_2(Z) of half-twists (Artin generators) whose squares are pure-braid generators of P_3/Z = F_2.
errors: The displayed formulas eps_inf(l_0) = l_0 l_1 l_0^{-1}, eps_inf(l_1) = l_0 describe the uncorrected element int(l_0) sigma_inf (alpha = 0), not the final eps_inf. For alpha = 1 one gets instead eps_inf(l_1) = l_1^{-1} l_0 l_1. This is a provisional line, not a real error.

The intermediate crossed-out lines contain slips: the first expansion is marked 'Non !', and an alternative exponent form l_0^{1-alpha} l_1^{2-alpha} l_inf^alpha = 1 is abandoned. The final result alpha = 1 is correct; directly, eps_inf^2 = l_inf^{2 alpha - 1}.

ideas.what: Extension of S_3 by pi_1(P^1 - {0,1,inf}) inside Aut(pi), with lifts sigma_i of the transpositions; S_3 symmetry of the tripod
ideas.modern_name: Orbifold pi_1 of the j-line, i.e. profinite PSL_2(Z) = Gamma(2)/±1 extended by S_3 (equivalently B_3/center over P_3/center)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein, Fricke); in the profinite/Galois context Grothendieck, Ihara, Drinfeld (GT, 1990)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (S_3 symmetries, Teichmüller tower, M_{0,4}, M_{1,1})

ideas.what: Square roots eps_i of the inertia generators l_i, normalised via eps_i = l_{i+1} sigma_i l_i so that eps_i^2 = l_i
ideas.modern_name: Cusp (parabolic) generators of PSL_2(Z) of width 2 relative to Gamma(2); images of half-twists in B_3/Z

deep.surprise_reason: A routine normalisation computation in the profinite completion of PSL_2(Z) = extension of S_3 by the free group on two generators. It is correct and well known in substance, part of Grothendieck's 1981 groundwork for the Teichmüller tower and GT-type considerations, but contains nothing absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: First line likely reads: 'Comme int(l_0)σ_∞ fixe l_∞ (mais n'est peut-être pas ... ), on doit le multiplier à droite par un int(l_∞^α)'.
'doit être ε_∞^2 = l_∞' is more plausibly 'doit écrire'/'doit équivaloir ε_∞^2 = l_∞', i.e. the condition imposed on α.
In 'identifiant K à un ss-groupe de Aut(K)', K denotes the group π of the previous page.
The final crossed 'OK' line should read l_0 l_1 l_0 l_0^{-1} l_1^{-1} l_1 l_1^{-1} l_0^{-1} = 1 (the α = 1 check), consistent with the image.
